description:
Hit while closing out the 2026-08-13 GH-issue session. Own dogfooding, on the
freshly-installed 0.1.4.

    $ timeout 90 bn sync
    Terminated

Ninety seconds, no output, killed by timeout. Every OTHER command on the same
store in the same minute was instant: `bn list` (35 rows), `bn count` (49),
`bn close` x4, `bn create` x6 — all returned immediately. So the store is
healthy and the daemon is up; it is `sync` specifically that does not come back.

`bn sync` is documented as "Wait for debounced sync flush to complete". Nothing
should have been pending — the writes had already landed and
`.beads/issues.jsonl` showed no diff afterwards.

Host: Arch, Linux 7.1.7, kopi-beans 0.1.4 from crates.io, remote is
https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/kopitiam (a real network remote).

Suspects, in order:
  1. Now that push actually goes over the network via the system git binary
     (0.1.3, GH#19), a flush may be waiting on a real remote round-trip with no
     timeout and no progress output. Would make this a REGRESSION introduced by
     the push fix — before it, non-local push failed fast with an error.
  2. Waiting on a debounce/flush condition that is never signalled when there is
     nothing to flush, i.e. it hangs precisely in the no-op case.
  3. Daemon lock contention, the bd-cni family.

What to establish first: run it with `-v`/`-vv`, and check whether the hang
survives `--no-push`-equivalent conditions or a `file://` remote. If it IS the
network round-trip, `sync` needs a timeout and a progress line — a command whose
whole job is "wait" must say what it is waiting for, same lesson as bd-pl2.

Whatever the cause, `sync` must not hang unbounded and silent. An agent running
it in a session-close script blocks forever.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-08-13. Two independent hang paths, both real, both need fixing.

PATH 1 — the deadlock (primary suspect for what I hit):
  daemon/git_lane.rs fail_sync():
      sync_in_progress = false;
      consecutive_failures += 1;
      dirty = true;              // keep dirty so we retry after backoff
  daemon/runtime/server/waiters.rs flush_sync_waiters() releases a waiter ONLY when
      !dirty && !sync_in_progress
  So a sync that FAILS sets dirty=true, the waiter's release condition can never be
  true, and the retry fails again -> dirty=true again. Backoff caps at ~32s and
  retries forever. The SyncWait waiter is parked FOREVER. bn sync blocks until you
  kill it. There is no timeout anywhere: client send() has none, the daemon parks
  the responder in a HashMap with no deadline, and nothing ever tells the waiter
  'the sync keeps failing'.

PATH 2 — no timeout on the push subprocess:
  git/gix_compat.rs subprocess_push() does cmd.output() with NO deadline. If git
  stalls (TCP connect hangs, TLS handshake stalls, ssh waits), sync_in_progress
  stays TRUE forever and the same waiter never releases. GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0
  stops credential PROMPTS but does nothing about a stalled transfer.

Both end in the same place: bn sync never returns and never says why.

WHAT THE FIX MUST DO (not just add a timeout — the deadlock is the real bug):
  1. Wake waiters on FAILURE, not only on success, and tell them it failed:
     consecutive_failures + the last error. A command that waits must be able to
     report 'still failing' instead of hanging.
  2. Deadline on the SyncWait waiter, with --timeout on bn sync.
  3. Deadline on the git push subprocess. Consider git-native
     http.lowSpeedLimit/lowSpeedTime for stalled transfers PLUS a hard process
     watchdog (covers ssh and pre-transfer hangs).
  4. On timeout, print the actual state: dirty, sync_in_progress,
     consecutive_failures, last error, remote URL. Exit non-zero.

title: kopi-beans: 'bn sync' hangs past 90s on a store with no pending work (Linux, 0.1.4)
